newsitem.title: USA: Northern Natural seeks expansion approval.
newsitem.headline: Northern Natural seeks expansion approval.

text.p: Northern Natural Gas Co said Monday it has filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for approval of an expansion designed to increase peak day firm transporation service by about 350 million cubic feet per day between 1997 and 2001.
The Enron Corp subsidiary said the project, Peak Day 2000, is expected to increase contracted market area peak day firm entitlements by 10 percent and cost about $105 million.
The planned peak day entitlement increases are 244 million cubic feet in 1997, 32 million in 1998, 31 million in 1999, 21 million in 2000 and 20 million in 2001, the pipeline said.
Northern Natural said the project is concentrated in its upper midwest markets in Nebraska, Iowa, South Dakota, Minnesota and Wisconsin.
Precedent agreements providing for long term contracts have been executed by expansion participants which include local distribution companies, marketers and industrial end-users, the pipeline said.
The major expansion is in response to requests received during an open season held earlier this year, it added.
The company said the 1997 in-service target date is November 1, assuming timely regulatory approval. Remaining increments will be phased in annual on November 1 through the year 2001.

Northern Natural Gas is a 16,987 mile system extending from Texas to Michigan and the Canadian border with capacity to move 4.3 billion cubic feet of natural gas daily into the upper midwestern market. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
